channel.title: DeepStack
channel.description: DeepStack is an independent publication on the AI economy: the capital, the chips, the power and the people betting on all three. Sharp analysis, sourced numbers, a clear verdict.

item.title: The Backlog Is Not the Quarter
item.description: AI suppliers report record order books. DeepStack reads the near book as revenue, the far book as a promise and the margin as the number that arrives last.

item.title: DeepStack Weekly No. 1: The riskless bond pays more than the stock market
item.description: 5 of 5 notes under pressure. 10-year Treasury at 5.29%. The Bubble Is in the Denominator.

item.title: The Bubble Is in the Denominator
item.description: AI spending made the market look cheaper. The harder test is whether those profits survive depreciation, weak productivity and a bond market financing the buildout.

item.title: Habit Was the Moat. Agents Are Draining It.
item.description: Meta’s Muse is testing whether AI shopping agents can reroute spending, squeeze weak subscriptions and expose which moats still hold.

item.title: AI Lenders Are Financing the End of Scarcity
item.description: AI capacity is scarce, but lenders are financing the supply that could erase that scarcity before hyperscaler cash flow catches up.

item.title: The Fed Hiked. The Long End Still Climbed.
item.description: The Fed raised short rates, but long yields climbed. AI financing now sits inside a bond market priced by growth, deficits and a thinner buyer base.

item.title: Power Doesn’t Depreciate. Its Premium Moves.
item.description: AI’s scarcity rent is shifting from chips to permitted, delivered power—but execution, politics and demand can still break the trade.

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Are Not the Same Business
item.description: OpenAI is losing pricing power while Anthropic still monetizes enterprise coding, exposing the risk of treating two very different labs as one AI bet.

item.title: AI Spending Has Met Its First Real Bill
item.description: AI’s buildout is entering its first financing test: spending outruns cash flow, investors have separated the winners from the believers, and the next budget will expose who is right.

item.title: The Machines Will Work. The Debt Might Not.
item.description: AI demand is holding up, but vendor guarantees, short-term premiums and widening credit concessions expose a fragile financing chain.

item.title: SpaceX Is Funding an AI Bet Before the Proof
item.description: SpaceX’s IPO funds a credible AI buildout, but the stock is pricing future capacity before deployment, revenue quality and Starlink coverage are proven.

item.title: Nvidia’s Demand Is Real. Its Financing Is Fragile.
item.description: Nvidia’s demand looks real today, but private credit, slow-to-build working compute and fast obsolescence make the revenue recurrence less secure than the backlog suggests.
